# Pettifer

## Overview

- **Age:** Middle-aged  <sub>[v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007)</sub>
- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v2 c1 P4](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0004)</sub>
- **Origin:** New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Farmer  <sub>[v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007), [v2 c17 P8](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0008), [v2 c18 P20](../source/v02-c18.md#nw-v02-c18-p0020)</sub>

## Appearance

Mr. Pettifer is a low-statured, heavy-set man who is bald except for a thin strip of hair encircling his ears, making him very sensitive about his hairless scalp. He is not considered good-looking, and his eyes are blue and bulging.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c1 P21](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0021), [v2 c1 P22](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0022)_

## Personality

Known as an eccentric, candid, and cranky individual, Mr. Pettifer prides himself on speaking his mind bluntly and truthfully without minced words. He is touchy, quick to ignite into outbursts of anger, and frugal, yet he possesses an underlying kindheartedness and good nature once understood. Though prone to giving unvarnished critiques of creative works and life, he forms deep, lasting bonds of friendship with neighbors like Nell Harcourt and displays a humorous, pragmatic outlook.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P8](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0008), [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c1 P15](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0015), [v2 c1 P22](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0022), [v2 c1 P26](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0026), [v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023), [v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c9 P5](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0005), [v2 c9 P6](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0006), [v2 c9 P11](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0011), [v2 c30 P1](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0001), [v3 c11 P50](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0050), [v3 c12 P39](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0039), [v3 c12 P41](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0041), [v3 c12 P74](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0074), [v4 c3 P3](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0003)_

## History

After moving to Brierley from New Brunswick, Mr. Pettifer acquired a reputation for eccentricity, frugality, and unusual domestic habits. He initially feuded with neighbor Nell Harcourt over her Jersey cow repeatedly breaking into his oat field. After Nell accidentally sold his cow to a buyer, she visited his home with a pink-frosted nut cake as a peace offering, leading to a warm resolution and the beginning of a close friendship between them. Over time, Mr. Pettifer offered practical, unvarnished advice to Nell regarding her teaching plans and story writing. When a thunderstorm struck the area, lightning killed his beloved parrot Nutmeg, leaving him deeply saddened. His estranged wife Emily later arrived in Brierley after seeing a newspaper prank, resulting in their domestic reconciliation, a newly cleaned house, and his return to church attendance. He continued to take a keen interest in Nell's life and writing, ultimately being invited as one of her cherished guests to her wedding.

## Background by volume

- originally from New Brunswick before buying Robert Bell's farm in Brierley  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- attended a school where the master flogged him daily  <sub>[v2 c4 P36](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0036)</sub>
- was given a foul-mouthed parrot named Nutmeg by his brother, a sailor  <sub>[v2 c1 P10](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0010), [v2 c3 P6](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0006)</sub>
- separated from his wife Emily years prior after marital disputes before her unexpected return  <sub>[v2 c25 P43](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0043), [v2 c25 P55](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0055)</sub>

## Quotes

> Patience isn't a virtue anymore, miss.  <sub>[v2 c1 P13](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0013)</sub>
